title: Kavero’s Brilliant Inventions
author: Prabhjee Kaur

stories.title: The Bed-Making Machine
stories.summary: Kavero builds a contraption to straighten his blanket, but Fozzy settles on it. Granny pulls, Poppy doubts, and the invention needs to accommodate a very comfortable puppy.

stories.title: A Pocket Too Far
stories.summary: Kavero designs a pocket big enough for his diary and every useful object. As Granny adds compartments, the pocket becomes harder to wear than the things it carries.

stories.title: The Slipper Shuttle
stories.summary: A cardboard trolley delivers Granny’s slippers—unless Fozzy retrieves them first. Kavero gives the eager puppy a delivery job of his own.

stories.title: The Page-Turning Problem
stories.summary: A hands-free page turner turns three pages, then none, while Miette sits on the instructions. The friends forget to ask whether Granny actually enjoys using it.

stories.title: The Rolling Pencil Rescue
stories.summary: A pencil keeps rolling off Granny’s table, prompting an increasingly elaborate rescue system. Mr Bell helps the children notice the slope, and Kavero creates a pencil parking space.

stories.title: Granny’s Third Hand
stories.summary: Granny is holding so many project parts that Kavero builds her an extra hand. When the holder grips the wrong things, Poppy notices Kavero’s own hands are available.

stories.title: The Plant-Watering Parade
stories.summary: Homemade channels should water several pots at once, but one pot gets nearly everything. Granny pours, Pip predicts waterfalls, and Mr Bell helps Kavero rethink the route.

stories.title: The Quiet Snack Carrier
stories.summary: Kavero pads a snack box so Fozzy cannot hear it travelling to the garden. The puppy arrives anyway, revealing that sound is not his only clue.

stories.title: The Wind-Proof Picnic
stories.summary: Everyone helps secure a picnic against the wind, including things people still need to use. Granny’s request for lunch becomes the invention’s most important test.

stories.title: The Question Catcher
stories.summary: Kavero builds a funnel-and-paper machine to catch questions before he forgets them. Granny listens into the wrong end, and a simpler way of saving questions emerges.

stories.title: The Sock-Sorting Slide
stories.summary: A slide should send matching socks into matching baskets, but socks do not travel according to colour. Millie enjoys the deliveries while Kavero rethinks what the machine can sort.

stories.title: The Bubble Parking Bay
stories.summary: Kavero wants to park a bubble long enough to draw it. Granny’s spotted glasses and a wet-surface experiment reveal that keeping a bubble still is not the same as keeping it forever.

stories.title: The Rain Orchestra
stories.summary: Kavero arranges containers for rain to play a tune, then waits with Granny for the weather. The eventual performance is less orderly—and more interesting—than expected.

stories.title: The Cat Detour
stories.summary: Kavero creates an alternative perch to lure Miette off the work surface. The cat ignores every invitation, then claims the spot as soon as the children stop trying.

stories.title: The Hug Substitute
stories.summary: Kavero invents a cushion for Granny to hug when he is out. Testing it gives her what she loves most: an afternoon with him, followed by a hug no invention can improve.

stories.title: The Lost-Diary Detector
stories.summary: A worried Kavero tries to turn a cardboard tube into a diary detector. Retracing his steps finds the diary in yesterday’s clothes and inspires a useful place to keep it.

stories.title: The What-If Machine
stories.summary: A machine combines question slips into gloriously impractical invention ideas. Granny draws an unexpected combination, and Kavero opens his diary to begin wondering again.
